passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Speak to the Israelites and say to them, ‘When someone makes a special vow to the LORD involving the value of persons, if the valuation concerns a male from twenty to sixty years of age, then your valuation shall be fifty shekels of silver, according to the sanctuary shekel.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a message for the Israelites.
The LORD told Moses to speak to the Israelites.
The LORD said, “If someone makes a special vow to the LORD about the value of a person, follow these rules.
If the person is a male from twenty years old to sixty years old, set the value at fifty shekels of silver.
Use the sanctuary shekel for this value.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ דַּבֵּ֞ר אֶל־ בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם אִ֕ישׁ כִּ֥י יַפְלִ֖א נֶ֑דֶר בְּעֶרְכְּךָ֥ נְפָשֹׁ֖ת לַֽיהוָֽה׃ וְהָיָ֤ה עֶרְכְּךָ֙ הַזָּכָ֔ר מִבֶּן֙ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וְעַ֖ד בֶּן־ שִׁשִּׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה וְהָיָ֣ה עֶרְכְּךָ֗ חֲמִשִּׁ֛ים שֶׁ֥קֶל כֶּ֖סֶף בְּשֶׁ֥קֶל הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃

passages.text: Or if it is a female, then your valuation shall be thirty shekels.
passages.sermon:
God gave laws to Israel through Moses at Mount Sinai.
God told Moses to speak to the Israelites.
God gave instructions about making special vows to the LORD.
These vows involved assigning a value to a person.
If the person is a female,
then the value you assign is thirty shekels.
passages.original: וְאִם־ נְקֵבָ֖ה הִ֑וא וְהָיָ֥ה עֶרְכְּךָ֖ שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים שָֽׁקֶל׃

passages.text: And if the person is from five to twenty years of age, then your valuation for the male shall be twenty shekels, and for the female ten shekels.
passages.sermon:
God gave Moses instructions for the Israelites.
God described how to value people who make a special vow to the Lord.
If the person is between five and twenty years old, set the value by age and gender.
If the person is a male, the value is twenty shekels.
If the person is a female, the value is ten shekels.
passages.original: וְאִ֨ם מִבֶּן־ חָמֵ֜שׁ שָׁנִ֗ים וְעַד֙ בֶּן־ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וְהָיָ֧ה עֶרְכְּךָ֛ הַזָּכָ֖ר עֶשְׂרִ֣ים שְׁקָלִ֑ים וְלַנְּקֵבָ֖ה עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת שְׁקָלִֽים׃

passages.text: Now if the person is from one month to five years of age, then your valuation for the male shall be five shekels of silver, and for the female three shekels of silver.
passages.sermon:
This law describes the valuation of a person for a vow offering to the LORD.
The law applies to a person who is between one month and five years old.
If the person is a male, the value is five shekels of silver.
If the person is a female, the value is three shekels of silver.
passages.original: וְאִ֣ם מִבֶּן־ חֹ֗דֶשׁ וְעַד֙ בֶּן־ חָמֵ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֔ים וְהָיָ֤ה עֶרְכְּךָ֙ הַזָּכָ֔ר חֲמִשָּׁ֥ה שְׁקָלִ֖ים כָּ֑סֶף וְלַנְּקֵבָ֣ה עֶרְכְּךָ֔ שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת שְׁקָלִ֖ים כָּֽסֶף׃

passages.text: And if the person is sixty years of age or older, then your valuation shall be fifteen shekels for the male and ten shekels for the female.
passages.sermon: This law describes the value of a person who is sixty years old or older.\r\nIf the person is a male, set the value at fifteen shekels.\r\nIf the person is a female, set the value at ten shekels.
passages.original: וְ֠אִם מִבֶּן־ שִׁשִּׁ֨ים שָׁנָ֤ה וָמַ֙עְלָה֙ אִם־ זָכָ֔ר וְהָיָ֣ה עֶרְכְּךָ֔ חֲמִשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר שָׁ֑קֶל וְלַנְּקֵבָ֖ה עֲשָׂרָ֥ה שְׁקָלִֽים׃

passages.text: But if the one making the vow is too poor to pay the valuation, he is to present the person before the priest, who shall set the value according to what the one making the vow can afford.
passages.sermon:
A person may make a vow to the LORD.
Sometimes, the person making the vow is poor.
The poor person cannot pay the full amount set by the law.
The poor person must go to the priest.
The priest will see the person who made the vow.
The priest will decide a new value for the vow.
The priest will set the value based on what the person can afford.
passages.original: וְאִם־ מָ֥ךְ הוּא֙ מֵֽעֶרְכֶּ֔ךָ וְהֶֽעֱמִידוֹ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְהֶעֱרִ֥יךְ אֹת֖וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֑ן עַל־ פִּ֗י אֲשֶׁ֤ר תַּשִּׂיג֙ יַ֣ד הַנֹּדֵ֔ר יַעֲרִיכֶ֖נּוּ הַכֹּהֵֽן׃ס

passages.text: If he vows an animal that may be brought as an offering to the LORD, any such animal given to the LORD shall be holy.
passages.sermon:
A person may vow to give an animal to the LORD.
The animal must be one that can be offered as a sacrifice to the LORD.
Any animal given to the LORD in this way becomes holy.
The animal belongs to the LORD as a holy offering.
passages.original: וְאִם־ בְּהֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַקְרִ֧יבוּ מִמֶּ֛נָּה קָרְבָּ֖ן לַֽיהוָ֑ה כֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִתֵּ֥ן מִמֶּ֛נּוּ לַיהוָ֖ה יִֽהְיֶה־ קֹּֽדֶשׁ׃

passages.text: He must not replace it or exchange it, either good for bad or bad for good. But if he does substitute one animal for another, both that animal and its substitute will be holy.
passages.sermon:
A person may vow to give an animal as an offering to the LORD.
He must not replace that animal with another animal.
He must not exchange a good animal for a bad one.
He must not exchange a bad animal for a good one.
If he does substitute one animal for another,
then both the original animal and the substitute will be holy.
passages.original: לֹ֣א יַחֲלִיפֶ֗נּוּ וְלֹֽא־ יָמִ֥יר אֹת֛וֹ ט֥וֹב בְּרָ֖ע אוֹ־ רַ֣ע בְּט֑וֹב וְאִם־ הָמֵ֨ר יָמִ֤יר בְּהֵמָה֙ בִּבְהֵמָ֔ה וְהָֽיָה־ ה֥וּא וּתְמוּרָת֖וֹ יִֽהְיֶה־ קֹּֽדֶשׁ׃

passages.text: But if the vow involves any of the unclean animals that may not be brought as an offering to the LORD, the animal must be presented before the priest.
passages.sermon:
Some animals are unclean.
People cannot offer unclean animals to the LORD.
If someone vows an unclean animal, he must present the animal.
He must bring the animal before the priest.
passages.original: וְאִם֙ כָּל־ בְּהֵמָ֣ה טְמֵאָ֔ה אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹא־ יַקְרִ֧יבוּ מִמֶּ֛נָּה קָרְבָּ֖ן לַֽיהוָ֑ה וְהֶֽעֱמִ֥יד אֶת־ הַבְּהֵמָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

passages.text: The priest shall set its value, whether high or low; as the priest values it, the price will be set.
passages.sermon:
A priest must decide the value of the animal.
The priest looks at the animal.
The priest decides if it is good or bad.
The priest sets the price.
The price will be exactly what the priest decides.
passages.original: וְהֶעֱרִ֤יךְ הַכֹּהֵן֙ אֹתָ֔הּ בֵּ֥ין ט֖וֹב וּבֵ֣ין רָ֑ע כְּעֶרְכְּךָ֥ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן כֵּ֥ן יִהְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: If, however, the owner decides to redeem the animal, he must add a fifth to its value.
passages.sermon:
The owner may want to redeem the animal.
The animal is unclean.
The animal cannot be offered to the LORD.
The priest has set the animal’s value.
If the owner redeems the animal, he must pay more.
He must add one fifth to the value set by the priest.
passages.original: וְאִם־ גָּאֹ֖ל יִגְאָלֶ֑נָּה וְיָסַ֥ף חֲמִישִׁת֖וֹ עַל־ עֶרְכֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: Now if a man consecrates his house as holy to the LORD, then the priest shall value it either as good or bad. The price will stand just as the priest values it.
passages.sermon:
A man may choose to make his house holy to the LORD.
The man gives his house to God for a special purpose.
The priest must look at the house.
The priest decides if the house is good or bad.
The priest sets a value for the house.
The value depends on what the priest decides.
The price will be the amount the priest sets.
The price will not change.
The priest’s decision is final.
passages.original: וְאִ֗ישׁ כִּֽי־ יַקְדִּ֨שׁ אֶת־ בֵּית֥וֹ קֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וְהֶעֱרִיכוֹ֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן בֵּ֥ין ט֖וֹב וּבֵ֣ין רָ֑ע כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יַעֲרִ֥יךְ אֹת֛וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן כֵּ֥ן יָקֽוּם׃

passages.text: But if he who consecrated his house redeems it, he must add a fifth to the assessed value, and it will belong to him.
passages.sermon:
A man may consecrate his house to the LORD.
The priest will set the value of the house.
If the man wants to redeem his house, he must pay extra.
He must add one fifth to the value set by the priest.
Then the house will belong to him.
passages.original: וְאִ֨ם־ הַמַּקְדִּ֔ישׁ יִגְאַ֖ל אֶת־ בֵּית֑וֹ וְ֠יָסַף חֲמִישִׁ֧ית כֶּֽסֶף־ עֶרְכְּךָ֛ עָלָ֖יו וְהָ֥יָה לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: If a man consecrates to the LORD a parcel of his land, then your valuation shall be proportional to the seed required for it—fifty shekels of silver for every homer of barley seed.
passages.sermon:
A man may dedicate a piece of his own land to the LORD.
The priest must determine the value of the land.
The value depends on how much seed is needed to plant the land.
The standard is barley seed.
The price is fifty shekels of silver for each homer of barley seed required.
passages.original: וְאִ֣ם׀ מִשְּׂדֵ֣ה אֲחֻזָּת֗וֹ יַקְדִּ֥ישׁ אִישׁ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וְהָיָ֥ה עֶרְכְּךָ֖ לְפִ֣י זַרְע֑וֹ זֶ֚רַע חֹ֣מֶר שְׂעֹרִ֔ים בַּחֲמִשִּׁ֖ים שֶׁ֥קֶל כָּֽסֶף׃

passages.text: If he consecrates his field during the Year of Jubilee, the price will stand according to your valuation.
passages.sermon:
A man may consecrate his field to the LORD.
He may do this during the Year of Jubilee.
The Year of Jubilee is a special year in Israel.
In that year, the price of the field will be set.
The price will be according to your valuation.
Your valuation means the amount you have determined.
passages.original: אִם־ מִשְּׁנַ֥ת הַיֹּבֵ֖ל יַקְדִּ֣ישׁ שָׂדֵ֑הוּ כְּעֶרְכְּךָ֖ יָקֽוּם׃

passages.text: But if he consecrates his field after the Jubilee, the priest is to calculate the price in proportion to the years left until the next Year of Jubilee, so that your valuation will be reduced.
passages.sermon:
A man may consecrate his field to the LORD after the Year of Jubilee.
The priest must calculate the price of the field.
The priest uses the number of years remaining until the next Year of Jubilee to determine the price.
The priest reduces the valuation according to the years left.
The value becomes less because fewer years remain until the Jubilee.
passages.original: וְאִם־ אַחַ֣ר הַיֹּבֵל֮ יַקְדִּ֣ישׁ שָׂדֵהוּ֒ וְחִשַּׁב־ ל֨וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֜ן אֶת־ הַכֶּ֗סֶף עַל־ פִּ֤י הַשָּׁנִים֙ הַנּ֣וֹתָרֹ֔ת עַ֖ד שְׁנַ֣ת הַיֹּבֵ֑ל וְנִגְרַ֖ע מֵֽעֶרְכֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: And if the one who consecrated the field decides to redeem it, he must add a fifth to the assessed value, and it shall belong to him.
passages.sermon:
A man may consecrate his field to the LORD.
If this man wants to redeem his field, he must pay money.
He must pay the full assessed value of the field.
He must also add one fifth of that value to the payment.
After he pays this total amount, the field will belong to him again.
passages.original: וְאִם־ גָּאֹ֤ל יִגְאַל֙ אֶת־ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה הַמַּקְדִּ֖ישׁ אֹת֑וֹ וְ֠יָסַף חֲמִשִׁ֧ית כֶּֽסֶף־ עֶרְכְּךָ֛ עָלָ֖יו וְקָ֥ם לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: If, however, he does not redeem the field, or if he has sold it to another man, it may no longer be redeemed.
passages.sermon:
A man may consecrate his field to the LORD.
If the man does not redeem his field, the field remains consecrated.
If the man sells the field to another person, the field remains consecrated.
No one may redeem the field after it is sold to another person.
The field cannot be redeemed again.
passages.original: וְאִם־ לֹ֤א יִגְאַל֙ אֶת־ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה וְאִם־ מָכַ֥ר אֶת־ הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה לְאִ֣ישׁ אַחֵ֑ר לֹ֥א יִגָּאֵ֖ל עֽוֹד׃

passages.text: When the field is released in the Jubilee, it will become holy, like a field devoted to the LORD; it becomes the property of the priests.
passages.sermon:
The field is land that someone consecrated to the LORD.
The Year of Jubilee is a special time when property is released.
When the Jubilee comes, the field is released.
The field becomes holy to the LORD.
The field is like a field that is devoted to the LORD.
The priests receive the field as their property.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֨ה הַשָּׂדֶ֜ה בְּצֵאת֣וֹ בַיֹּבֵ֗ל קֹ֛דֶשׁ לַֽיהוָ֖ה כִּשְׂדֵ֣ה הַחֵ֑רֶם לַכֹּהֵ֖ן תִּהְיֶ֥ה אֲחֻזָּתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Now if a man consecrates to the LORD a field he has purchased, which is not a part of his own property, then the priest shall calculate for him the value up to the Year of Jubilee, and the man shall pay the assessed value on that day as a sacred offering to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
A man may buy a field that is not part of his family land.
If this man sets apart the field for the LORD, he makes it holy.
The priest will decide how much the field is worth.
The priest will count the value from that day until the Year of Jubilee.
The man must pay the full value on that same day.
This payment is a holy gift to the LORD.
passages.original: וְאִם֙ אֶת־ שְׂדֵ֣ה מִקְנָת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֕ר לֹ֖א מִשְּׂדֵ֣ה אֲחֻזָּת֑וֹ יַקְדִּ֖ישׁ לַֽיהוָֽה׃ וְחִשַּׁב־ ל֣וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֗ן אֵ֚ת מִכְסַ֣ת הָֽעֶרְכְּךָ֔ עַ֖ד שְׁנַ֣ת הַיֹּבֵ֑ל וְנָתַ֤ן אֶת־ הָעֶרְכְּךָ֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא קֹ֖דֶשׁ לַיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: In the Year of Jubilee the field shall return to the one from whom it was bought—the original owner of the land.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel the law of the Jubilee.
The Jubilee happened every fifty years.
In the Year of Jubilee, special rules applied to land.
If someone bought a field from another person, he did not keep it forever.
When the Year of Jubilee came, the field returned to the original owner.
The original owner was the person who first held the land as his property.
The buyer gave the field back to this original owner in the Jubilee year.
passages.original: בִּשְׁנַ֤ת הַיּוֹבֵל֙ יָשׁ֣וּב הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה לַאֲשֶׁ֥ר קָנָ֖הוּ מֵאִתּ֑וֹ לַאֲשֶׁר־ ל֖וֹ אֲחֻזַּ֥ת הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: Every valuation will be according to the sanctuary shekel, twenty gerahs to the shekel.
passages.sermon: Every valuation must use the sanctuary shekel.\r\nOne shekel equals twenty gerahs.
passages.original: וְכָל־ עֶרְכְּךָ֔ יִהְיֶ֖ה בְּשֶׁ֣קֶל הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים גֵּרָ֖ה יִהְיֶ֥ה הַשָּֽׁקֶל׃ס

passages.text: But no one may consecrate a firstborn of the livestock, because a firstborn belongs to the LORD. Whether it is an ox or a sheep, it is the LORD’s.
passages.sermon:
A firstborn animal belongs to the LORD.
No one may consecrate a firstborn animal to the LORD.
This rule applies to every firstborn of the livestock.
If the animal is an ox, it belongs to the LORD.
If the animal is a sheep, it belongs to the LORD.
The firstborn of the livestock is always the LORD’s.
passages.original: אַךְ־ בְּכ֞וֹר אֲשֶׁר־ יְבֻכַּ֤ר לַֽיהוָה֙ בִּבְהֵמָ֔ה לֹֽא־ יַקְדִּ֥ישׁ אִ֖ישׁ אֹת֑וֹ אִם־ שׁ֣וֹר אִם־ שֶׂ֔ה לַֽיהוָ֖ה הֽוּא׃

passages.text: But if it is among the unclean animals, then he may redeem it according to your valuation and add a fifth of its value. If it is not redeemed, then it shall be sold according to your valuation.
passages.sermon:
An unclean animal does not meet the requirements for sacrifice to the LORD.
A person may redeem an unclean animal.
He must pay the value you set for it.
He must also add one fifth of that value.
If he does not redeem the animal, then sell it.
Sell it for the value you set.
passages.original: וְאִ֨ם בַּבְּהֵמָ֤ה הַטְּמֵאָה֙ וּפָדָ֣ה בְעֶרְכֶּ֔ךָ וְיָסַ֥ף חֲמִשִׁת֖וֹ עָלָ֑יו וְאִם־ לֹ֥א יִגָּאֵ֖ל וְנִמְכַּ֥ר בְּעֶרְכֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: Nothing that a man sets apart to the LORD from all he owns—whether a man, an animal, or his inherited land—can be sold or redeemed; everything so devoted is most holy to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
A man may set apart something he owns for the LORD.
He may set apart a person, an animal, or his inherited land.
He cannot sell what he sets apart for the LORD.
He cannot redeem what he sets apart for the LORD.
Everything set apart in this way is most holy to the LORD.
passages.original: אַךְ־ כָּל־ חֵ֡רֶם אֲשֶׁ֣ר יַחֲרִם֩ אִ֨ישׁ לַֽיהוָ֜ה מִכָּל־ אֲשֶׁר־ ל֗וֹ מֵאָדָ֤ם וּבְהֵמָה֙ וּמִשְּׂדֵ֣ה אֲחֻזָּת֔וֹ לֹ֥א יִמָּכֵ֖ר וְלֹ֣א יִגָּאֵ֑ל כָּל־ חֵ֕רֶם קֹֽדֶשׁ־ קָֽדָשִׁ֥ים ה֖וּא לַיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: No person set apart for destruction may be ransomed; he must surely be put to death.
passages.sermon:
God gave laws to Israel.
\r\nGod commanded about people set apart for destruction.
\r\nNo person set apart for destruction can be ransomed.
\r\nHe must be put to death.
passages.original: כָּל־ חֵ֗רֶם אֲשֶׁ֧ר יָחֳרַ֛ם מִן־ הָאָדָ֖ם לֹ֣א יִפָּדֶ֑ה מ֖וֹת יוּמָֽת׃

passages.text: Thus any tithe from the land, whether from the seed of the land or the fruit of the trees, belongs to the LORD; it is holy to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
A tithe is a tenth part.
The tithe comes from the land.
The tithe can come from the seed of the land.
The tithe can come from the fruit of the trees.
The tithe belongs to the LORD.
The tithe is holy to the LORD.
passages.original: וְכָל־ מַעְשַׂ֨ר הָאָ֜רֶץ מִזֶּ֤רַע הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ מִפְּרִ֣י הָעֵ֔ץ לַיהוָ֖ה ה֑וּא קֹ֖דֶשׁ לַֽיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: If a man wishes to redeem part of his tithe, he must add a fifth to its value.
passages.sermon: A man may want to redeem part of his tithe.\r\nHe must add one fifth to its value.
passages.original: וְאִם־ גָּאֹ֥ל יִגְאַ֛ל אִ֖ישׁ מִמַּֽעַשְׂר֑וֹ חֲמִשִׁית֖וֹ יֹסֵ֥ף עָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: Every tenth animal from the herd or flock that passes under the shepherd’s rod will be holy to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God gave a command to the Israelites through Moses at Mount Sinai.
God required a tithe from the herd and the flock.
The shepherd counts the animals as they pass under his rod.
Every tenth animal belongs to the LORD.
The tenth animal is holy to the LORD.
passages.original: וְכָל־ מַעְשַׂ֤ר בָּקָר֙ וָצֹ֔אן כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ יַעֲבֹ֖ר תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑בֶט הָֽעֲשִׂירִ֕י יִֽהְיֶה־ קֹּ֖דֶשׁ לַֽיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: He must not inspect whether it is good or bad, and he shall not make any substitution. But if he does make a substitution, both the animal and its substitute shall become holy; they cannot be redeemed.’ ”
passages.sermon:
God gave commandments to Moses for the Israelites on Mount Sinai.
These commandments include rules about tithing animals.
Every tenth animal from the herd or flock belongs to the LORD.
The owner must not check if the animal is good or bad.
The owner must not substitute one animal for another.
If the owner does substitute one animal for another, both animals become holy.
Both the original animal and its substitute belong to the LORD.
No one can redeem either animal.
passages.original: לֹ֧א יְבַקֵּ֛ר בֵּֽין־ ט֥וֹב לָרַ֖ע וְלֹ֣א יְמִירֶ֑נּוּ וְאִם־ הָמֵ֣ר יְמִירֶ֔נּוּ וְהָֽיָה־ ה֧וּא וּתְמוּרָת֛וֹ יִֽהְיֶה־ קֹ֖דֶשׁ לֹ֥א יִגָּאֵֽל׃

passages.text: These are the commandments that the LORD gave to Moses for the Israelites on Mount Sinai.
passages.sermon:
The LORD gave commandments to Moses.
Moses was the leader of the Israelites.
The LORD gave these commandments for the Israelites.
The LORD gave these commandments on Mount Sinai.
passages.original: אֵ֣לֶּה הַמִּצְוֺ֗ת אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־ מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל בְּהַ֖ר סִינָֽי׃
